subject: Emotions
title: The Caste System and Untouchability
description: One-minute skill: The Caste System and Untouchability.

hook.text: For thousands of years, 'untouchable' castes in India were forced to do work others found disgusting.

buildup.text: Cleaning toilets, handling dead bodies, tanning leather—all assigned to Dalits based on purity beliefs.

discovery.text: The caste system fused disgust with social hierarchy. Contact pollution justified permanent exclusion.

twist.text: Ambedkar, himself a Dalit, wrote India's constitution and outlawed untouchability. The law changed; feelings lagged.

climax.text: Disgust-based hierarchies are the hardest to dismantle because the emotion feels natural, not learned.

punchline.text: The cruelest hierarchies feel obvious to those on top.

quiz.question: Who wrote India's constitution and outlawed untouchability?
